title: Throughput Attestation Ledger and Customer Witness Tests
creator: Ava Chen
description: Create an auditable, reproducible ledger of throughput attestations for Dedicated Capacity customers plus a scripted "customer witness" test flow. The ledger captures deterministic workload signatures, probe parameters, raw telemetry hashes, and the resulting SLA metrics so customers and support can independently verify throughput guarantees. This ticket covers the harness orchestration, metrics signing, customer witness runbook, and acceptance criteria for sign-off.
motivation: Customers buying Dedicated capacity need a deterministic, tamper-evident record proving the fleet met the promised throughput/SLOs under the agreed workload profile. Existing load suites are useful internally but lack an easy-to-run customer-facing witness flow and a standardized attestation artifact that ties inputs -> telemetry -> results.
design_notes: Key concepts: (1) Workload Signature: a compact descriptor (seed, tenant-slice mix, prompt shapes, seq length distribution, QPS profile) that can be re-run; (2) Deterministic Replayer: seeded RNG and fixed timing to make runs reproducible; (3) Telemetry Hashing: canonicalize token-level timings and hash for ledger immutability; (4) Attestation Envelope: JSON file with signature, run metadata, and links to raw logs; (5) Customer Witness Flow: short guided execution the customer can run or watch with support and produce a matching attestation. Trade-offs: we balance reproducibility vs realism by capturing both deterministic baseline and a second randomized replay to show variance bounds.
acceptance_criteria: Ledger format v1 defined and documented in Confluence with schema and example
Deterministic replayer implemented and can reproduce a run within a 2% throughput variance on the same fleet topology
Telemetry hashing implemented and verified (SHA-256) with canonicalization rules
Automated attestation envelope produced and signed by platform key after each certified run
Customer witness runbook created (step-by-step, <30 minute guided flow) and internal dry-run completed with Support
PR to GitHub for replayer and ledger producer merged with tests and example artifacts
Console view: attestation artifact accessible from Dedicated customer consoles with download and verification instructions
implementation_steps: Spec ledger schema and canonicalization rules (Confluence: /docs/dedicated/throughput-ledger-v1)
Extend existing load-harness to accept a deterministic seed + workload signature descriptor
Add instrumentation hooks to record per-request timing, queue wait, grpc payload sizes, and token emit timings
Create canonicalizer that strips non-deterministic fields and orders records for hashing
Implement telemetry hashing and sign attestation envelope with platform signing key (KMS integration)
Build a short customer witness orchestration script (Python CLI) with interactive prompts and automated artifact upload
Expose attestation artifacts in Console and emit an event to the customer audit log
Run internal bench: three repeated runs on staging fleet topology; capture variance and tune replayer timing parameters
Prepare Support runbook and schedule two pilot witness sessions with selected customers
runbook_quick_commands: # Generate workload signature from template: python tools/workload_gen.py --template tenant_mix_10_90.json --seed 42 --out sig.json
# Start deterministic replayer against staging: ./harness/replay --sig sig.json --target staging-dedicated --concurrency 128 --duration 1800
# Verify attestation locally: python tools/verify_attestation.py attest-<id>.json --public-key keys/platform_pub.pem
telemetry_contract: Fields recorded: timestamp_utc, request_id, tenant_id (bucketed), model_name, seq_len, tokens_emitted, latency_ms (queue+service), gpu_util_pct, host_id
Sampling rule: record every request for certified runs; redact user payloads and only store prompt hashes
Canonical ordering: sort by request_id, then timestamp; normalize timestamps to ms since run-start
Hash algorithm: SHA-256 over newline-separated canonical records
Retention: raw artifacts kept for 30 days; ledgers and signed envelopes retained per customer contract
customer_witness_flow: Pre-run: exchange workload signature and run window with customer; confirm topology snapshot and tenant isolation level
During run: customer joins Zoom (optional) or is given ephemeral access link; Support triggers replayer and watches Console metrics
Post-run: attestation artifact uploaded to customer portal; Support walks customer through verification CLI or web verifier
Sign-off: customer confirms attestation matches expected run and accepts SLA evidence; record acceptance in Customer Onboarding ticket
risks_and_mitigation: Non-determinism due to cloud placement changes: mitigation - capture node topology snapshot and require fleet topology lock for certified runs
Large artifact size for long runs: mitigation - use compressed canonical records and include pointer to raw logs stored in GCS
Customer distrust of platform-signed artifact: mitigation - provide public key, an offline verifier, and allow witness to run the same replayer
KMS signing lifecycle issues: mitigation - rotate signing keys per policy and provide key fingerprint in envelope
